65-75% of arbitrary words of comparable frequency clear the same bar, and
synthetic profiles carrying no information about the word -- only which
creator used it and how often -- clear it at 88%. False-positive rate RISES
with occurrence mass (49% below 600 occurrences, 84% at 4,000-10,000), and
the pinned terms sit in the 1,800-18,500 band. Clearing the bar is
NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT: it detects side-linked structure, much of which
is topic and creator rather than contested meaning. Full measurements and
the candidate remedies in docs/research/2026-07-29-bar-specificity-*.md;
no remedy is adopted yet, so every verdict here rests on the bar as it is.

The modern pastor sits at the head of a congregation, but their authority is local, not theological. Their day-to-day work is the work of a practitioner, managing the life of the church, sustaining weekly community rhythms, performing rituals, supervising volunteers, offering comfort, and packaging moral encouragement as theology. They are the custodians of tradition, not the creators of it.
